candidates.rationale: Weakest part is the short 5-day TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5) denominator: this exact chassis already has 3 archive members differing only by denominator (TS_RANK(dv,5)/raw dv/TS_STD(close,21)), so per rule 10 a bare window retune would just collide again. Swapping the axis from time-series rank to cross-sectional rank (CS_RANK) changes what's being normalized against (own history vs same-day peers) rather than just retuning a parameter.

Rule 3 says don't touch TS_MIN($low,21) or its window, vary the ratio's structure instead. The weak link is that TS_MAX draws from $high while the rest of the ratio is close/low based; swapping the ceiling reference from $high to $close changes what defines the top of the range without touching the flagged TS_MIN leaf, and avoids wrapping the whole parent subtree (which would trip archive_subtree since this expression is itself an archive member).

TS_STD($close,21) is the flagged-saturated component (dead at w in {5,10,21,63} per prior rounds). Swapping the vol measure from price-level std to return std changes it from a price-scale statistic to a scale-free volatility statistic, a structural field change rather than a window retune on the saturated leaf.

ABS(eps) is the weakest piece: it's a linear magnitude transform, and MIN(eps,0)/close plus ABS(eps)/book_per_share are already archived, closing the obvious denominator swaps. Wrapping ABS in SQRT keeps the non-negative magnitude idea but reshapes it nonlinearly, which reorders the cross-sectional ranking once divided by an independently-varying $close, unlike a same-sign MAX(eps,0) swap which would track ABS almost exactly for the eps-positive majority of the panel.

The generic $close normalizer is the weakest component; per rule 5 this X is closed for several partners already. book_per_share is an untried denominator for the bare (non-ABS) ratio (only the ABS-wrapped version with book_per_share exists in the archive), giving eps a book-value scale instead of a price scale.

Raw $dollar_volume as a bare denominator is the weakest, least-shaped component in this saturated chassis (3 sibling archive members already share the ($close-$low)/TS_MEAN(...,10) skeleton). LOG compresses the dollar-volume scale nonlinearly, changing the ratio's magnitude profile across small vs large names rather than just re-windowing or rank-transforming it (which the sibling family already covers).

Working-memory rule 1 flags TS_DELTA($close,3) directly: a <=5-day raw price delta is return-equivalent and failed cheap_screen twice this round. The 21-day retune of this same leg is already an archive member, so lengthening further to 42 both clears the flagged short-window failure mode and avoids the already-claimed 21-day variant.

Rule 5 says fuse eps with a second operator rather than keep hunting for a fresh X in the RANK(eps)-RANK(X) difference form. Swapping the outer combinator from subtraction to multiplication is a one-node structural change that produces a materially different combined distribution than a rank difference (memory notes rank differences dilute IC toward a fixed blend of the two legs' own IC).

Same family as the sibling parents; rule 5 flags this exact X (($close-$low)/$close) as the point other variants (e.g. /$high) already collide against, so the difference structure around it is the weak spot, not the ratio itself. Switching '-' to '*' is a minimal structural edit that avoids the already-explored rank-difference space for this X.

Rule 2 warns against touching the DELAY lag itself; the archive independently confirms this chassis already has two DELAY-lag variants (lag 1 and lag 21) under TS_MEAN, so the lag axis is mined. The weak component is instead the outer TS_MEAN aggregator: swapping it for TS_STD changes the statistic from the ratio's level/drift to its dispersion, a structural change orthogonal to the already-saturated lag parameter.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.
